clauses.reason: Whole order (single operative paragraph, offsets 0-647 of the held text jobs/app-executive-orders/output/texts/executive-order-8584-exemption-frank-burke-from-compulsory-retirement-for-age.txt): signed November 7, 1940. The recital finds that the public interest requires that the employee be further exempted from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year, and the operative sentence, under section 204 of the act of June 30, 1932 (47 Stat. 382, 404), further exempts Frank Burke from compulsory retirement for age for a period of one year ending December 31, 1941. That exemption is the order's only command and it carries its own fixed term. The recital names the earlier exemption Executive Order No. 8302 of December 12, 1939; those are earlier instruments, not events on this order. First end: the order's own stated end, December 31, 1941 (operative sentence: "for a period of one year ending December 31, 1941."). The stated date is recorded inclusive (the exemption runs through the end of December 31, 1941); the exclusive reading, under which it ends when December 31, 1941 begins, is the alternative. The date is the end of the stated term, not a record of separation or death; no such record is held. Later event, not an end: Executive Order 9002, signed December 29, 1941, further exempts the same person; its recital names this order ("Executive Orders No. 8302 of December 12, 1939, and No. 8584 of November 7, 1940") and its operative sentence runs "ending December 31, 1942". Like this order it has no effective-date wording, so I read it as effective on signing. MOMMSEN-I recheck: Own APP see. / GPO sec.; selected later EO 9002 APP duplicates 47 Stat. 382, 404, whereas GPO prints it once. Both copies identify the same statute and section; repetition adds no legal term. This is a disclosed nonmaterial duplication, not a claim of verbatim agreement.
